deposit_profile: A deposit address is one customer's: everything it sends goes to the wallets of one exchange (a sweep into a hot wallet), few outside addresses ever pay it, it never swaps on a DEX, and it is no token, pool, router or smart account.
hint: Answer: write every address in full (0x plus 40 characters), also when it repeats one named earlier and also when the user asks for shorter ones (name them instead); a transfer moves tokens, so write "tokens worth about N USD", never "sent N USD" or a $ figure; never draw the flows in text, ASCII or Mermaid, the host draws them. 0x9866f491a33ffb6a9301863d5db9743f794784fa is not in the Chain Insights Graph of robinhood: no flow touches it. Say so in one line, and check the network and the address with the user: name no other network yourself, and say nothing about what the check covers. A claim that it is an exchange deposit address is unproven on this network: never repeat it as a fact. Asked how a deposit address behaves, what makes an address one or what rules one out, answer with deposit_profile.
